newsitem.title: USA: MEMC sees earnings improve in Q4.
newsitem.headline: MEMC sees earnings improve in Q4.

text.p: MEMC Electrobnics Materials Inc said Thursday it expected to improve its bottomline by the end of the year as the market for silicon wafers is recovering, despite its reporting nearly flat earnings in the second quarter.

"We expect third-quarter net results will be similar to results from operations in the second quarter," said chief executive Ludger Viefhues in a statement. "Looking ahead to the fourth quarter, we expect to see some improvement in financial results as the market continues its recovery.

MEMC posted net earnings of $3.8 million, or $0.09 a share, in the quarter ended June 30. The earnings included a $3.4 after-tax gain, or $0.08 a share, for selling its Santa Clara, Calif., silicon wafer plant.
The company earned $400,000, or $0.01 a share, excluding the gain, compared with a net of $46.5 million, or $1.12 a share, in the second quarter of 1996.
Sales dropped to $245.8 million from $324.3 million over the same period. MEMC said its gross margins were 12.5 percent in the quarter, compared with 28.0 percent a year ago.

Compared to the first quarter (when the company posted a $2.8 million loss, or a loss of $0.07 a share), however, sales rose 11 percent. MEMC attributed the sales growth to strong demand for its 8-inch prime and epitaxial wafers, which are building blocks of semiconductors.
The company's stock closed at 38-1/2 Thursday, up 1/8 and close to its 52-week high of 39-1/8.
